summary: Implemented the post-amendment T012 contract for the V4 math port: (1) removed the float API entirely from src/robinhood_lp/protocol/math.py (deleted sqrt_price_x96_to_price and price_to_sqrt_price_x96 and dropped them from __all__) and from src/robinhood_lp/protocol/__init__.py (imports and __all__ entries both gone); (2) added round_up: bool keyword-only parameters to get_amount0_delta and get_amount1_delta in src/robinhood_lp/protocol/math.py (default False preserves current behaviour) and implemented the Solidity ceil-rounding branches — get_amount0_delta roundUp uses ((liq << 96) * (pb - pa) + (pa * pb) - 1) // (pa * pb), get_amount1_delta roundUp uses (liq * (pb - pa) + 2**96 - 1) >> 96 (the actual V4 SqrtPriceMath formula is mulDivRoundingUp(liq, pb - pa, Q96) — note the task's hint about ((liq << 96) * (pb - pa) + pb - 1) // pb would not match the existing floor fixture, while the formula above reproduces it exactly); (3) updated tools/oracle/src/MathOracle.sol so amount0Delta and amount1Delta accept a bool roundUp parameter and forward it to SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta / getAmount1Delta; (4) updated tools/oracle/test/MathOracle.t.sol so the _emitAmount0Delta / _emitAmount1Delta helpers take a bool roundUp, log_named_bool it, and the test calls them twice (roundUp=false then roundUp=true) for every (pa, pb, liquidity) triple — twelve vectors per function family total; (5) extended tests/fixtures/protocol/math_vectors.json by adding a roundUp=true mirror for every existing amount_deltas triple (six new entries) and a round_up boolean field on every entry so the test can route the value through to get_amount*_delta; (6) created src/robinhood_lp/presentation/__init__.py and src/robinhood_lp/presentation/prices.py hosting the single Decimal-typed display helper to_display_price(sqrt_price_x96: int, decimals0: int, decimals1: int) -> Decimal per ADR-009 — integer-only path, 18 fractional digits, and the only V1 module permitted to import Decimal; (7) updated tests/test_protocol_math.py so test_amount_deltas_match_oracle reads round_up from the fixture and forwards it via round_up= to get_amount0_delta / get_amount1_delta — no coverage was deleted; (8) added tests/test_protocol_display.py with eight tests pinning to_display_price closed-form values for the (0,0) and (6,18) decimal cases, the invertibility property for swapped decimals, type/range rejection (uint160 overflow, negative sqrt, decimals out of [0, 36], non-int args), and an AST-based property test that fails if anyone re-adds a float Name / Attribute / arg inside src/robinhood_lp/protocol/. The task hint 'for get_amount1_delta this is ((liquidity << 96) * (pb - pa) + pb - 1) // pb' would not reproduce the existing floor fixture (it produces values ~10^15× too large); the actual V4 SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta formula is mulDiv(liquidity, sqrtPriceBX96 - sqrtPriceAX96, FixedPoint96.Q96), i.e. (liquidity * (pb - pa)) >> 96 for floor and ((liquidity * (pb - pa)) + 2**96 - 1) >> 96 for roundUp. The Python implementation matches the existing Foundry-emitted floor fixtures and reproduces the corresponding roundUp values, so the implementation is correct, but the task hint and the implementation diverge; a Triage reviewer should confirm Owner sign-off on the actual formula before T013 depends on it.

to_display_price rounds to 18 fractional digits via Decimal.quantize; for extremely large or small sqrt_price_x96 values near the uint160 boundaries (e.g. MIN_SQRT_PRICE_X96 or MAX_SQRT_PRICE_X96 - 1) the human-scale ratio can hit 10**36 or 10**-36 after the decimal shift, and the rounding quantum (1e-18) is still small enough to keep the result accurate at 18 fractional digits. The current 60-digit working precision is comfortable for that range; if a future V2 needs more than 18 fractional digits it must also raise getcontext().prec above 60 in this module.
